messages:
maria: heads-up — partner-prod marketplace images started failing after we rolled the new driver/CUDA stack. repro is FP16 convs OOM on resnet workload. seeing this only with CUDA 12.2 + driver 535.x pinned in their marketplace image.

cheng: got logs? any kernel oops or is it user-space OOM?

maria: early traces look like cuBLAS workspace size blowup. snippet from their CI: ```RuntimeError: cuBLAS status CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED at conv_fp16_forward``` plus nvidia-smi shows GPU mem spike then reset.

sam: @maria can you drop the full nvidia-smi and docker runtime flags? need to check pinned driver vs container toolkit. often it's a mismatch between driver ABI and container runtime.

maria: attaching what partner pasted (edited for brevity): ```nvidia-smi 535.86.10  Driver Version: 535.86.10  CUDA Version: 12.2``` container built with base image `ubuntu:22.04 + cuda-toolkit 12.2`. runtime flags: `--gpus all --shm-size=1g`.

eric: quick thought — if driver 535 introduced a vmalloc regression for certain kernel modules, that could explain sudden allocation failures. we had one internal report last month on microcode/driver mismatch. tagging @olivia for marketplace gating rules.

olivia: if partner marketplace image is pinned to the 535 driver we need a short playbook: 1) patch their image to fallback to older driver ABI (12.1) OR 2) publish a hotfix package we can recommend and coordinate with partner. which is faster?

cheng: fastest path is a hotfix container that forces smaller cuBLAS workspace env: `export TF_CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_SIZE=...` — but that's a brittle workaround. better long-term: coordinate with HW partner to confirm driver kernel modules and push driver micropatch.

sam: operational plan: (A) create a canary image with CUDA 12.1 and push to partner staging (B) reproduce perf/regression matrix (C) if fails, escalate to HW partner for driver hotfix. I can take (A) and (B) today.

maria: thanks. partner asked about delaying their joint announcement scheduled for next week — they prefer not to go live until we confirm stable stack. they want a comms ETA.

olivia: tell partner we aim for 48–72 hours for a canary report. we should also schedule a 30-min sync with partner engineering + HW partner. I'll coordinate.

eric: one more ask: can we add a short regression test to our marketplace gating CI that runs a small FP16 conv stress test on any new pinned driver? will catch this early.

maria: yes, good call. I'll open a gating ticket. ticket: `PARTNERS-4372` (will paste link).

deploy-bot: build kicked: `marketplace-canary:cuda-12.1-fallback` started (ci-run-9982).

sam: I'll attach repro steps and logs to PARTNERS-4372 once canary finishes. will ping here with results. :thumbsup:

cheng: if we get flaky results, we should consider temporary marketplace policy: no driver pinning without compatibility sign-off. not sure if partner contract allows, but ops should discuss.

olivia: agreed, we'll loop in partnerships legal if needed. for now, don't block the announcement until the canary completes. keep communication transparent.

maria: perfect — will update partner with 48–72h ETA and link PARTNERS-4372. thanks everyone.
